Can biodiverse playgrounds change immunity?

A 28-day daycare intervention links greener play environments with microbiome and immune markers.

Our everyday environments are designed. What can this published study actually tell us about their relationship with human health and the brain?

The study

A Finnish intervention studied 75 children aged three to five across ten daycare centers, adding biodiversity-rich materials to some play areas.

The findings

Over 28 days, microbial communities and selected immune-regulation markers changed. The study did not demonstrate prevention of disease or changes to the brain.

What this means for architecture

Schoolyard landscapes can shape microbial contact, making biodiversity relevant to architectural health research.

Conclusion

The evidence points to an important research question, not a universal design rule. Better controlled and longer-term studies are needed.

Roslund et al. (2020)

Biodiversity intervention enhances immune regulation and health-associated commensal microbiota among daycare children. Science Advances 6(42), eaba2578
